name: Jason Marsh
summary: Director of Technology at a nonprofit serving people with disabilities and older adults. 13+ years in IT, the last six in assistive technology and five leading teams. Restructured AT billing and grew annual service revenue from $17K to over $200K within a year. Designs, ships, and operates production software by directing AI coding agents (Claude Code), including WhatCanHelp, a free assistive-technology discovery site covering thousands of products. ATACP-certified (CSUN).

projects.name: WhatCanHelp
projects.desc: (whatcanhelp.com) - free assistive-technology discovery site for families, clients, and AT professionals who otherwise search vendor catalogs one at a time. Specified and shipped a freeform needs intake that returns a matched shortlist, complexity ratings so users know what setup a device needs, state-by-state borrowing and funding directories, and PDF reports for funding meetings and IEP appendices. Chose batch AI classification with prompt caching to keep a catalog of thousands of products affordable to maintain, with schema checks against fabricated product data. Built with AI coding agents; Node/Express + SQLite, self-hosted and in production.

projects.name: RadioGridXL
projects.desc: - internet radio for older adults and people with disabilities, deployed at my organization and piloted with older adults. Large buttons, no accounts or ads, screen-reader support, and low-vision, high-contrast and night themes. Designed a technician-only settings panel so staff set up stations from a curated directory without exposing that complexity to the listener.

projects.name: ButtonGriddle
projects.desc: - visual choice boards for tablets: each button is a photo of the person's own item and a phrase spoken aloud, with a Yes / No / Not sure screen so staff can check understanding. Staff and families build boards in a passcode-protected edit mode. Offline-first with no accounts; everything stays on the device. In beta.

projects.name: MCP Servers
projects.desc: - custom Model Context Protocol servers connecting Claude agents to self-hosted apps and everyday tools, with guardrails: hooks, sandboxing, approval gates on actions with side effects, and prompt-injection containment. In daily use.
